  • Startup splash. index.html itself contains #starting (data-splash="1"): a pure-CSS hourglass (.hourglass, two border triangles in a frame; the top one fades while the bottom one fills, then the glass turns over) and "Starting labmill…" in an aria-live="polite" status. It is visible on the first paint, before app.js or the Wails runtime load; the CSP stays strict (no inline style or script). main.go builds the runtime with launch.BuildWithProgress, whose Progress callback reports launch.StartLoadingSettings ("Loading your settings…"), StartOpeningDatabase, StartLoadingSkills and StartReady. Each step is emitted as labmill:startup ({step}) and stored in State.Step, so a page that loads late starts with the current one. After 10 s on the splash a second line says "This is taking a while. Still waiting for: loading skills (14 s)." (before the first step: "Labmill to start"); it counts again from the first-run form's submit. The chat replaces the splash as soon as the page has its Go bindings (phase "starting"): the input works at once, the status line shows the startup step, and a message sent before the runtime exists waits in gate.Send (a running turn) and is forwarded once. labmill:ready sets the status line. The runtime starts before the window on Windows (a second launch is detected with otherInstanceRunning first). Windows exe flags: -trimpath -s -w (smaller, faster loader). WebView2 uses one fixed user-data folder, %LocalAppData%\labmill\WebView2 (webviewUserDataPath); the old default folder (%AppData%\labmill-gui.exe) is left behind, never deleted.
  • Native start splash on Windows. The page-level splash above only exists once the window and WebView2 are up; before that (loader, antivirus scan of a new exe, Go init, tray, Wails) Windows showed nothing, and the tray's message loop ends the app-starting cursor at once. So main starts a native splash right after the helper-subcommand check and before the tray and wails.Run (startSplash in splash_windows.go; splash_other.go is a no-op). It is a borderless popup (WS_POPUP|WS_BORDER, WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW so no taskbar button, NOACTIVATE, not topmost (the new main window covers it), shown with SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE so it never takes focus), 360x120 at 96 DPI scaled by the system DPI, centered on the rectangle the saved window geometry (read alone from gui.json by savedWindowGeom) opens in, else the primary work area (splashRect, clamped into the work area). It shows the app icon (exe resource 3, cmd/labmill-winres), "Starting labmill…", a self-drawn moving bar (a progress control's marquee needs common controls v6, which needs a manifest) and the app-starting cursor (WM_SETCURSOR), in the dark or light colours of the Windows app theme (AppsUseLightTheme). It runs on its own locked OS thread with its own message loop. closeSplash (thread-safe, idempotent: posts WM_CLOSE) is called from OnDomReady, showWindow (tray open), OnShutdown and after wails.Run returns; the window also closes itself after 60 s. Skipped (splashWanted): --tray starts (also when a setup form would show), the self-test and smoke test, and a second launch that only hands over: Wails exits that process inside Run, so main probes the single-instance mutex first (otherInstanceRunning, the same cheap probe the tray uses) and shows no splash, so there is no flash. Timing marks: "gui: splash shown", "gui: splash closed". The Windows self-test checks splashStarts == 0 and that no splash step is in the timing list; the visible splash itself is not checked by any test.
  • Tray. The tray icon is started before wails.Run (it needs nothing from Wails) with the tooltip and status line gui.TrayStarting ("Labmill is starting…"); the status loop is refreshed at once when the runtime is ready or failed (not only every 10 s), and the tooltip becomes gui.TrayTooltip ("Labmill: no jobs running · …"). A tray click before the window exists is remembered and shown in OnStartup; the tray's Quit does nothing until the window exists.
  • "Working…" row. #working sits under the conversation (outside the role="log" region, so its updates aren't read as chat): a small hourglass, #working-text (role="status", aria-live="polite") and #working-time. send() shows "Working…" synchronously when a new turn starts (not when the message is only queued), so it appears before Go answers; labmill:turn restarts it. labmill:step ({text}, from agent.EventStep via gui.Bridge) and a tool call ("Running …") set its text; labmill:text hides it (a later step or tool call shows it again); labmill:done hides it. After 5 s it shows the seconds since it appeared (a 250 ms timer), so it never looks frozen. Cancel stays available, transfers keep their own progress row (#xfer), and #progress now shows only the latest labmill:notify line (the tool activity moved into the row).
  • Where the steps come from. agent.Agent emits EventStep agent.StepWaitingForClaude before every model call. Below the agent, launch's stepTracker emits "Connecting to …" while connCache.client opens an SSH login (not for a cached client, and never for the background job monitor, which uses existingClient). When such a part ends the tracker puts the previous step back ("Waiting for Claude…", "Running cluster_info…"), unless a newer step replaced it or the reply text already started; it learns the agent's steps by wrapping Agent.OnEvent. Approvals are unchanged: steps never ask or decide anything.
  • Reduced motion. @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) sets animation: none on the hourglass and its triangles: a still hourglass with the sand on top.
  • Terminal. The TUI's status bar shows its Bubbles spinner followed by the same texts (model.step: "Working…", the EventStep texts, "Running …") and the elapsed seconds after 5 s; while a turn runs a shorter key hint makes room for it, and a NotifyMsg follows the step instead of replacing it. Startup in the terminal is not shown step by step (launch.Build).

items.title: Settings page
items.text:
The Settings page shows and edits every setting Labmill keeps; see the user page docs/user/settings.md for what each section does.

  • Opening. The header's gear button (#settings-open, shown once the page reaches ready or failed: app.js calls labmillSettings.enable()), the tray menu's "Settings…" and, on macOS, File > Settings… (Cmd+,) both show the window and emit labmill:open-settings. frontend/settings.js hides #main (or #fatal) and shows #settings; "Back to chat" or Esc outside a form returns and focuses the message box. The section list is a role=tablist (automatic activation: ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End move and open, only the selected tab is in the Tab order); the section is the role=tabpanel. Everything is built with createElement/textContent; the documentation address is a <code> field, never a link. Approval, login and sign-in dialogs still cover it (#app is inert under the overlay).
  • Binding. SettingsAPI (cmd/labmill-gui/settings.go, window.go.main.SettingsAPI) is a separate bound struct from PageAPI, so each script reaches only its own methods: Get, SaveSite, SaveCluster, RemoveCluster, SaveHost, RemoveHost, SetStartInTray, SetRunWithoutAsking, ApproveAll, SetApproveAll, JobsWidth, SetJobsWidth, AutoDownload, SetAutoDownload, SetNotifyJobEnd, SetEmailOnJobEnd, ResetNotices, MoreClusterPlan, AddMoreCluster, OpenLogsFolder, Diagnostics. The Folders section reuses PageAPI.Folders/PickFolder/SetFolder (same rules as the + menu) and refreshes the chat's chips (window.labmillApp.refreshFolders).
  • Rules. The logic is in internal/settings (testable without the desktop tag). Get reads local files only (no network, no login). Saves return a settings.Result: errors ({field, message}, the clusters.yaml key such as ssh_host or s3.bucket, or alias/hostName/user/port/proxyJump) shown under their fields with aria-invalid, or error, or message. Clusters are checked with config.FieldErrors (the rules of config.Validate, now tied to cluster index and field), the site with site.Get, SSH connections field by field with sshconfig.Host.Validate plus "host name required".
  • Writes. clusters.yaml is edited on the YAML node tree (config.SetSiteYAML, PutClusterYAML, RemoveClusterYAML): only touched keys change, comments and order stay, new keys go in the usual order, and the result must pass config.Parse. Before the first write of a session the file is backed up once (config.Backup: clusters.yaml.labmill-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>[-n], O_EXCL, 0600, never overwriting), then written atomically with 0600 (config.WriteFile). SSH connections go only to Labmill's file: sshconfig.PutLabmillHost rewrites the HostName/User/Port/ProxyJump lines of one Host block and leaves every other line, or appends a Render block (then EnsureInclude); RemoveLabmillHost drops one block. The user's ~/.ssh/config is read with sshconfig.ListHosts and never written; adding an alias it defines is refused. An alias can't be renamed, and one used by a cluster or as a jump host can't be removed. "Log out" is not offered: the helper has no request to close one login (logins end 10 minutes after the last client).
  • Restart. The running session loaded clusters.yaml and the SSH settings at startup, so every save of those says "Restart Labmill to apply" and the page shows a banner (View.restart). There is no restart button: quitting from the tray and starting again is the single-instance-safe path.
  • App. "Start in the tray when I log in" uses the tray's startAtLogin (autostart + gui.json) and updates the tray checkbox (tray.SetStartAtLogin); "Show the one-time tips again" clears Prefs.TrayNoticeShown and calls Lifecycle.ResetNotice.
  • Diagnostics. settings.View.Diagnostics(): version and platform, the broker URL (if any) without user info, query or fragment, the institution, clusters (no AWS profile or KMS key), connections (no user names) and the file paths. The page shows the exact text it copies (md.js copyText). "Open logs folder" uses gui.OpenFolder on the folder of labmill.log.
  • Terminal. /settings (tui.Options.Settings) prints settings.View.Text(): the same values without secrets and the file paths; it never starts a turn.
  • Self-test. The self-test writes a fixture (clusters.yaml with comments, Labmill's and a user SSH file) under labmill-selftest-folders/settings next to the executable (overwritten each run; backups accumulate there, nothing is deleted) and stubs every outside effect (autostart, folder opener, broker URL with user info and a query). selftest.js opens Settings with the gear, walks the section list with the keyboard, saves an invalid ssh_host (inline error, field focused, nothing written), fixes and saves it, checks the SSH, Folders (data first), App and About sections and that the copied diagnostics hold nothing secret-looking, then leaves with Esc. Go then checks the saved value, the kept comments, one backup equal to the original, mode 0600 and the untouched user SSH file.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
page (frontend/*)  <->  gui.App / gui.Bridge (internal/gui)  <->  launch.Runtime (internal/launch)
  • Decide(id string, approve bool, edited, reason string) error answers an approval; reason is the optional text typed with a decline (trimmed, textsafe.Clean, newlines collapsed to spaces, capped at 500 runes; ignored on approve). The dialog's "Tell Labmill why (optional)" input never takes the initial focus and Enter in it does nothing; Esc declines with whatever is typed.
  • Choose(id string, index int, other string, skip bool) error answers a labmill:choice dialog ({id, question, options: [{label, description}], allowOther}, sent for the ask_user tool): skip skips; otherwise a non-empty other is the typed answer (cleaned like a decline reason, needs allowOther); otherwise index is the 0-based option. Go side: gui.Bridge.Pick. A known ID is answered exactly once even on invalid input (answered skipped, with an error). The dialog's first option has the initial focus; Up/Down move between the options and the "Other" input, Enter picks the focused option, 1-9 pick directly, Esc and the Skip button skip.
  • The page calls bound methods at window.go.main.PageAPI.* (Send, Cancel, Unqueue, JobAction, Decide, Choose, Answer, Jobs, Status, Folders, PickFolder, SetFolder, DropFolder, OpenJobFolder, SelfTest, SelfTestReport), window.go.main.Setup.* (NeedsSetup, SubmitUsername, State) and, from the Settings page, window.go.main.SettingsAPI.* (see "Settings page"), and listens with window.runtime.EventsOn. PageAPI is a small struct that forwards to gui.App; gui.App itself is not bound, because Wails binds every exported method and would expose Shutdown to the page. PageAPI.Status returns the runtime's status line once it is ready.
  • index.html carries a Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (xterm.js writes <style> elements;style-src-elemneeds the WKWebView of macOS 12.3 or newer, older systems lose the terminal's colors and layout); img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'); Wails needed no extra allowance on Linux (WebKitGTK). There is no inline script or style. Dropped file contents never reach the page: only paths, and only from drops onto the chat input box after the user picks data or code, are used (see "Folders and Open folder"; drops elsewhere reach the runtime JS on macOS and Linux but are discarded), and the page cancels every dragover and drop.
  • Chat: assistant replies are Markdown rendered by frontend/md.js with DOM nodes only (no innerHTML; links and images become plain "text (url)" with no href/src; raw HTML stays text). While a reply streams it is re-rendered at most every 50 ms, and at once before a tool line and at the end of the turn. Each tool call is one collapsed <details> line ("load_skill · 4.2 KB", "job_logs · 120 lines") that expands to the full text in monospace; errors show their first line. Font sizes are in rem (chat 1rem, code 0.875rem in a monospace stack). The job panel is at least 20rem wide; its cells never wrap and end in an ellipsis, with the full text in a tooltip.
  • The prompt is always available. The input and Send are never disabled. gui.App.Send starts a turn when idle. While a turn runs, it queues the text instead: one message, and a newer Send replaces it. The queued message starts as the next turn when the running one ends, also after Cancel. Unqueue drops it, and Shutdown drops it too. The page doesn't guess what happened from Send's return. It follows events: labmill:turn ({text}) when a turn starts (the page then shows the user message and the busy state), labmill:queued ({text}, "" = nothing queued) for the "Queued, sent when this reply ends" line with its Remove button, and labmill:done when a turn ends. labmill:queued is emitted under the App's lock, so it always comes before the labmill:turn that sends that text. While busy, the Send button reads "Queue". Esc in the chat input does nothing special.
  • Job notices: gui.Bridge.JobNotice (part of launch.UI, called by the background job monitor) emits labmill:job ({text}, cleaned). The page shows it as a small .msg.system line, placed above a reply that is still streaming so the reply stays whole, and refreshes the job list at once.
  • Job buttons: JobView.Actions lists the buttons for each job. Status and Logs appear once the job is submitted (it has a remote ID). Fetch appears when the job is completed or failed and has a remote folder. Cancel appears while it is submitted, pending or running. Open folder appears once it is fetched with a local folder; it opens the folder (PageAPI.OpenJobFolder) instead of sending a message. They are real <button>s in a row under the job, with textContent labels and an aria-label naming the job. A click calls PageAPI.JobAction(id, action), which checks the action against the job's current actions and sends a plain chat message through Send: "Show the status of job #12", "Show the last lines of the log of job #12", "Fetch the results of job #12" or "Cancel job #12". The message is queued while busy, so everything goes through the agent and its approvals (Cancel still asks). The table is rebuilt only when the job list changed, and the focused button keeps the focus.
  • Dialogs: input is ignored for 500 ms after a dialog opens and again after the window regains focus; key repeats and clicks that began during the grace period are ignored. The title and buttons stay fixed while the body scrolls. A labmill:dismiss event closes dialogs that Go abandoned. When altered is set the page warns that the text was cleaned for display.
  • gui.Bridge implements launch.UI: approvals, choices and login questions become labmill:approval, labmill:choice and labmill:prompt events with an ID, and wait for exactly one Decide, Choose or Answer; the turn ending answers them (declined, skipped, canceled) and sends labmill:dismiss. Text is cleaned with textsafe.Clean before it leaves Go, and the page uses textContent only.
  • main.go builds the runtime with launch.BuildWithProgress (startup steps, see "Busy feedback") in a goroutine after startup. On first run (and when clusters.yaml names no known home institution, launch.NeedsHomeChoice, which also sets State.Note to launch.HomeInstitutionNote) its setup step blocks until the page submits the form (Setup.SubmitSetup: an empty or unknown institution is refused, a not-listed institution needs a login host, launch.HostsRequired; the account name is validated with launch.ValidUsername). It then sends labmill:ready or labmill:fatal; Setup.State lets a page that loaded late catch up.
  • Until the runtime is ready, a small gate stands in for the session and job store: a turn ends at once with "Labmill is still starting up", and Jobs returns the same error.
  • Closing the window goes through gui.Lifecycle (see "Tray and closing the window"): with a tray icon up it only hides the window. Quitting (the tray's Quit, or a close without a tray) goes through gui.Closer: OnBeforeClose returns at once (Windows calls it on the UI thread), the window is hidden, and App.Shutdown runs in the background (cancel the running turn, wait up to 10 s, decline pending dialogs, close the runtime) before the app quits. Wails' Quit re-enters OnBeforeClose, which then allows the close. If shutdown hangs for 30 s, the hidden process exits.
  • Terminal. The header's Terminal button, Settings > Clusters and the jobs panel's "Terminal here" open xterm.js tabs wired to a login-node shell (frontend/terminal.js, internal/gui/terminal.go); see ssh.md "Desktop terminal".

items.title: Where knowledge lives
items.text: Labmill's know-how comes from two places: the generic skills and the site profiles. This page states the rules for which knowledge goes where.

items.title: The rules
items.text:
1. Site-specific information lives only in sites/<domain>/. Only the public sites/generic/ fallback is in this repository. Profiles for real institutions are not part of the Labmill client; they are kept and shipped apart from it. Site-specific means anything that is true of one institution or one of its clusters, and not of research computing in general:
    • Slurm configuration: partitions, queues, QOS, accounts, limits, and how they are configured.
    • Software: where it can be found, what is already installed (modules, versions, images, drivers, CUDA), and container registries.
    • Access: how to log in, bastion and login hosts, transfer hosts, 2FA, proxies, and how to get an account.
    • Storage: data storage paths and their specific configuration (quotas, purge rules, scratch areas).
    • Hardware and support: GPU and node inventories, documentation and help-desk URLs.
    • Implicit facts: a number, model name or anecdote that only one site has, even without its name. Examples are a node's core count, the site's CUDA floor, or "it converged on GPU X but not Y" where X and Y are one site's GPUs.

  2. All generic knowledge lives in the skills (skills/).

    • Slurm manuals and best practices.
    • General research computing: virtual environments, conda, Jupyter notebooks, containers, POSIX file systems, storage tiers, SSH, shell hygiene, data transfer and credentials.
    • Research computing support: how to get help and how to write a good ticket.

    A site profile holds only the site's values, and points to the generic skill for everything else. 3. No site-specific information may ever appear in the skills. That covers skills/ in full, its provenance notes included. It also applies to Labmill's runtime code and embedded data (system prompt, tool descriptions, catalogs, defaults, UI text), to the public sites/README.md, and to all documentation. These read site values from Site.yaml / Cluster.yaml at run time, or use neutral examples (example.edu, bigcluster, /data/mygroup). 4. The README and the docs stay anonymous. README.md, CLAUDE.md and everything under docs/ name no institution, host, cluster, person or path of a real site. 5. Skills hold all the logic. A Claude Code user who installs the generic skills plus their site skill gets everything Labmill knows. Every change to domain logic also goes into the skills, with the shell commands a Claude Code user would run.

items.title: How it stays enforced
items.text:
• The leak test (internal/site/leak_test.go, TestGenericSkillsHaveNoSiteFacts) checks the embedded generic skills against every term derived from the site profiles that are present, plus curated forbidden_terms for implicit facts.
  • The drift test (internal/app/skillmap.go) ties each typed tool's logic to a skill section.
  • Every feature's acceptance includes "skills updated". The reviewer checks both directions:
    • no site facts in skills, code or docs;
    • no generic teaching in a site profile.

items.title: Security
items.text: This page lists the protections that exist in the code today, with where to find them. It is a summary, not a guarantee, and some items are listed as open at the end. The design rules are in CLAUDE.md.

items.title: Approvals
items.text:
• Every upload, job submission, cancellation and download is a gated tool. The loop builds a Proposal, asks the Approver and only then calls Run. With no approver, a gated tool fails (ErrNoApprover). (internal/agent)
  • Integrity re-check. Each gated tool's Run rebuilds the proposal from the same input and the current store, and refuses unless Summary and Details equal the ones the user approved ("this job changed since you approved it"). submit_job compares against the drafted script that was shown, then submits the user's edit or that exact script. A job that already has a remote ID can't be uploaded to again, and once a script is drafted its cluster can't change. (internal/app/tools.go)
  • The approval modal defaults to Decline, shows the summary and buttons at all times while details scroll, refuses to show a partial approval (a window too small), and ignores typed-ahead keys for half a second after opening. An edited script is submitted as shown, with a warning when the editor displays tabs or control characters differently. (internal/tui/approval.go, ui.go)
  • Skills are guidance only and never override approvals. The skill preamble tells Claude to use typed tools and never install software. (internal/skill, app.SkillPreamble)

items.title: What Claude can see
items.text:
• Claude gets file metadata (paths, names, sizes, counts) and small previews (data files: at most 20 lines and 4 KiB from the start; documentation and code files such as README*, scripts and build files: pages of at most 200 lines and 16 KiB, files up to 1 MiB, with the values of credential-looking keys such as password, token and api_key hidden; binary files refused). find_local_data and preview_file only look under LocalRoots (the home folder). (internal/app/localdata.go)
  • Privacy rules, one shared check for finding, previewing, staging and for download targets: no path component starting with .; ~/Library on macOS and AppData on Windows are off limits; Windows hidden-attribute entries are refused; files that look like secrets are never listed, previewed or staged (id_*, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, *.kdbx, *.keychain*, names containing "credential", "secret", "password" or "passwd", .netrc, .env*). Names are matched after Unicode case folding. (internal/app/privacy.go)
  • Remote side is not restricted (owner rule). The privacy rules above protect the user's own computer. On a cluster, remote_command has no path limits and no refusal lists: the account's permissions, enforced by the system administrators, decide. Read-only commands run at once, except a content-printing one (cat, head, tail, file -z) that names a sign-in secret by name (SSH private key, .netrc, cloud credentials, *.pem/*.key, histories; symlinks, hard links, /proc/*/environ and tokens inside ordinary files are not detected), which asks first and warns that the content goes to Claude (a credential-leak guard, not a limit). The output of those commands also goes through redactSecrets, as preview_file does. Any other command shows its exact line for the user's approval (consent, not a restriction), unless the user turned on the setting "Run commands on the cluster without asking" (off by default, gui.json): then those commands run at once, but a secret-file print still asks, and malformed argv is still rejected. Argv-only quoting, no terminal, closed stdin, timeout and output caps remain as mechanics. The exception to closed stdin is the optional script field: multi-line shell code is sent on stdin to bash -s (or another interpreter named in argv), is always shown in full for approval (also in auto-run mode it still asks when its words name a sign-in secret file, and an auto-run's output is redacted), and never enters the command line. A command that submits a job (sbatch, srun) is not refused; its result carries a hint to use submit_job.
  • Approve everything automatically. A user setting (gui.json approveAll, off by default, banner while on) makes agent.AutoApprover (wrapped around the front end's Approver in launch.Build, so the GUI, the TUI and the tests share it) approve each Proposal at once and unedited, then emit EventAutoApproved (chat line "Auto-approved: ", plus a line in labmill.log). On is read per proposal (settings.AutoApproveAll). It does not apply to: a Proposal with Secret set (today remote_command naming a sign-in secret file, remoteProposal), ask_user (agent.Chooser), and the SSH logins (sshx.Prompter), which are a separate interface that never pass through it. A new proposal kind whose content goes to Claude from a secret must set Secret. The decision carries Decision.Auto: remote_command then applies the run-without-asking safeguards (output redacted, remoteAutoNote first), and the loop prefixes every other automatically approved result with agent.AutoApprovedNote so Claude knows nobody reviewed it. The labmill.log line holds only the tool name and a short line redacted by app.RedactLine (credential keys and --token/--password/--key style arguments). The setting is a superset of runWithoutAsking, which stays for users who only want commands auto-run.
  • Stalled reads. A read on a network mount that stopped answering, or on a cloud placeholder file ("files on demand"), can block for minutes and no context reaches it. find_local_data and preview_file therefore do their blocking open/read/stat in a goroutine (internal/stall) and stop waiting when the limit passes, answering "skipped: didn't answer within N s" (the walk of find_local_data returns what it found so far). The goroutine can't be cancelled and may finish later (its result is dropped and it closes its file); at most 32 such reads exist at once per limiter (the file tools share one; Limiter.Stuck() counts them), and while all slots are stuck, further reads are refused at once with a note telling the user to reconnect the drive and restart Labmill. Stat and readdir are covered too: find_local_data runs its folder resolution and walk under stall.Run. When the caller's context ends, Run returns ctx.Err(), not a stall. Privacy rules and results are otherwise unchanged.
  • Windows junctions. Since Go 1.23 filepath.EvalSymlinks doesn't resolve junctions (mount points), so a junction inside the home folder pointing at a private place would pass CheckFolder/insideRoots. The app's checks resolve paths through evalLinks (internal/app/pathresolve*.go): EvalSymlinks everywhere, and on Windows additionally GetFinalPathNameByHandle on a handle opened with FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS (the \\?\ prefix stripped). The Windows part is cross-compiled and the prefix stripping and wiring are unit-tested on Linux, but it needs a check on a real Windows machine (a junction made with mklink /J). stage_data resolves each named path through evalLinks and refuses one that leads out of the folder or into a private place; the Windows resolver fails closed (an existing path whose final path can't be had is refused). transfer.BuildManifest and the config/ssh-config code still use EvalSymlinks. Also to check on real Windows: a code or data folder saved in workspace.json by an older version holds the old EvalSymlinks result; on a mapped or subst drive the new resolver gives \\server\share\…, so such a folder silently drops out of the allowed list until it is chosen again (fails closed).
  • Staging doesn't follow symlinks, skips special files and hidden entries (reporting them), and rejects any path that resolves outside the root. (transfer.BuildManifest)
  • The system prompt tells Claude to treat file names, file contents, job logs and tool results as data, never instructions. This is a mitigation, not a boundary; the approvals are the boundary.

items.title: No shell, typed tools only
items.text:
• There is no shell tool. Claude can only call the registered typed tools, each with a fixed JSON schema. An unknown tool name is an error result. (internal/agent)
  • Backends build argument vectors themselves from validated fields and run them through a Runner. Remote runners pass backend.Quote(argv), which single-quotes every argument that isn't made of safe characters. The only free-form text, the approved job script, is passed as data (stdin or a file), never spliced into a command line. (internal/backend)
  • Quote and backend.SplitWords have a fuzz round-trip test (see Testing).
  • Download paths must be relative, without .. or control characters, and the local folder must be inside the results folder or a local root and pass the privacy rules. (app.fetchResults, transfer.cleanRel)

items.title: Validation of job specs
items.text: JobSpec.Validate fixes the format of every field: name [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}, partition and GPU type without a leading -, absolute WorkDir from a plain alphabet (it is written into #SBATCH lines), image names, environment variable names, no #SBATCH lines inside the command, no NUL bytes, no carriage returns, and no control, bidi, zero-width or other format characters in the command or environment values, so the text the user approves is what runs. Failures wrap ErrInvalidSpec. (internal/backend/backend.go)

items.title: Display sanitization
items.text:
• Text from Claude and from the cluster is sanitized before the TUI shows it: control characters, DEL, C1 controls, whole escape sequences (CSI, OSC including OSC 8 links, DCS), bidi controls, line separators and invisible operators are removed. Sanitizing works on complete strings, not streamed fragments, so a sequence split across deltas is still caught. (internal/tui/sanitize.go)
  • File names and paths in proposals have control and invisible characters replaced with ? before they are shown or sent to Claude. (internal/app/privacy.go)

items.title: SSH: host keys and two-factor
items.text:
• Go-native SSH, no OpenSSH binary. Host keys are checked against ~/.ssh/known_hosts. An unknown host is confirmed once by the user (the dialog default is No, and it shows the SHA256 fingerprint); a changed key is never overridable from the dialog: Labmill refuses and tells the user to contact HPC support (ErrHostKeyMismatch). RSA keys are used only with rsa-sha2-256/512, never SHA-1 ssh-rsa. (internal/sshx/sshx.go)
  • The password prompt is hidden and asked at most once per login; the password is not re-sent to a server that already rejected it, to avoid counting twice toward a lockout. Passwords and 2FA codes live only in memory for the login exchange and are never written to disk. The Duo push is chosen from the menu text, and a missing push ends in a clear two-factor error with the site's help text.
  • Host templates written to ~/.ssh/config.d/labmill are validated first, because a newline in a host name would inject directives into a file every ssh reads. The file is written atomically with mode 0600, and the Include line is added after a timestamped backup of the user's config. (internal/sshconfig)

items.title: The SSH helper
items.text:
• The helper socket lives in a directory created with mode 0700; the helper refuses a symlinked directory or one owned by another user (Unix), forces the socket to mode 0600, and holds a lock file (named after the versioned socket, ssh-v1.lock) for its lifetime so two helpers can't race to replace each other's socket. A stale socket is replaced only when nothing answers on it.
  • Its local SSH server uses an ephemeral host key. Upstream prompts are relayed to the foreground process; the helper has no UI of its own. It exits after 10 idle minutes. (internal/sshx/helper.go, lock_unix.go)
  • The job database, labmill.log and the helper directory are created with owner-only permissions where Labmill creates them. Tightening an already existing database file is a known follow-up.

items.title: Model access
items.text:
• By default the client calls the Anthropic Messages API with the user's own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The key is read from the environment, kept in memory only and never written to disk. The SDK is built with WithoutEnvironmentDefaults, so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and other ANTHROPIC_* variables can't send the key somewhere else. (internal/launch/model.go)
  • Without a key and without a broker, a client linked to a Labmill account (account.json) uses the Labmill test relay (owner decision 2026-10-26, testing only): the broker client against <link URL>/api/model (the URL saved at labmill login, so LABMILL_ACCOUNT_URL applies) with the program token as bearer token. The key, when set, always wins and never goes to Labmill. The server forwards with Labmill's key and stores no request text. (internal/launch/model.go chooseModel)
  • When a broker is configured (broker_url in Site.yaml or LABMILL_BROKER_URL), the client sends model calls there with the bearer token from LABMILL_BROKER_TOKEN. The broker client requires an https base URL (plain http only for loopback), ignores ANTHROPIC_* environment variables, and treats a stream that ends without message_stop as an error. (internal/broker)

items.title: Labmill account link
items.text:
• Off until the user pastes a program token (labmill login reads it from stdin, hidden on a terminal, never from argv; the GUI uses a password field). account.Login checks the form (lmt_, printable, under 100 characters) and calls GET /api/me before it saves anything; a refused token is not saved.
  • The token is kept in account.json next to clusters.yaml, written atomically with mode 0600 (config.WriteFile). This is the one secret the client keeps on disk; the client has no OS key store. It is never logged, put in labmill.log, shown on the Settings page or printed by whoami. labmill logout deletes the file.
  • The account URL is https://app.labmill.org, or LABMILL_ACCOUNT_URL (https, plain http only for loopback, as the broker). Redirects are not followed, so the bearer header can't go to another host.
  • What is sent and what never is: see Architecture. Only jobs that end after the link was made are sent.

items.title: Downloaded know-how and results
items.text:
• Skill bundles from a broker are used only after the version hash and every file's SHA-256 check out, are written atomically, and are never mixed mid-session; a failed check falls back to the embedded copy. The user's override folder always wins, so a bundle can't replace the user's own skills. (internal/launch/knowledge.go, internal/knowledge)
  • Downloaded results are compared with sha256sum run on the cluster over the transfer connection. A differing file is renamed <name>.mismatch and never deleted; where the check can't run, the result says the files were checked by size only. (internal/transfer/verify.go)

items.title: rclone isolation
items.text: rclone runs in-process as a library, never as a binary. Its config file path is /dev/null, so no config is read or written; every backend is built from a local option map seeded with defaults, not from RCLONE_* environment variables; and the global options and filter in each transfer's context are replaced with fresh defaults, so variables such as dry-run or exclude rules have no effect. rclone's own package init may still create an empty ~/.config/rclone directory. Skill override files are read through an os.Root so symlinks can't escape the directory, and are capped at 256 KiB. (internal/transfer/transfer.go, internal/skill)

items.title: Known gaps
items.text: • Tightening an already existing job database file to owner-only permissions is a known follow-up.

items.title: Sites: adding an institution
items.text: Labmill keeps everything that differs between institutions in site profiles under sites/<domain>/. Only sites/generic/ is part of this repository; profiles for real institutions are kept and shipped apart from the client. The skills in skills/ (slurm-user, research-computing) are generic and say "see your site skill" wherever a value differs per site. One set of skills serves Claude Code and Labmill; neither forks them.

items.title: What a site folder contains
items.text:
Facts that hold for the whole institution sit at the top of sites/<domain>/. Everything specific to one cluster sits in a cluster folder named after it, so Claude reads only the cluster it needs:

sites/example.edu/
  Site.yaml             institution-wide values for Labmill (hosts, 2FA)
  SKILL.md              the site skill, name: site-example-edu; indexes the cluster folders
  References/*.md       institution-wide facts: accounts, two-factor sign-in, the
                        shared login and transfer hosts, campus proxy, general
                        storage rules, documentation links
  QUESTIONS.md          open questions and unverified items (not embedded)
  SOURCE.md             optional: where upstream skill text came from (domain root only, not embedded)
  Evals/*.json          optional site-specific skill evals (not embedded)
  Diagrams/*.svg        optional architecture diagrams, plus a Diagrams/README.md
                        describing them (not embedded, not a skill reference)
  bigiron/              a cluster folder (here: a Slurm cluster)
    Cluster.yaml        the clusters.yaml template entry plus cluster hints
    References/*.md     partitions, GPUs, limits, modules, cluster paths
    QUESTIONS.md        optional, open questions about this cluster
    Evals/*.json        optional
    Diagrams/*.svg      optional (and Diagrams/README.md)

A cluster folder's name is lowercase letters, digits and - (at most 63 characters) and can't be references, evals, diagrams or tools. Labmill ignores folders whose name starts with _ (sites/generic/_cluster-template/ is a template to copy).

  • The folder name is the institution's internet domain, lowercase (example.edu, example.org).
  • SKILL.md has the usual frontmatter. name is site- plus the domain with dots replaced by dashes (site-example-edu). The description starts with " () specifics for HPC/Slurm (): …" and lists what the references cover, so Claude loads it whenever a site fact is needed. The body is short: an index of the cluster folders ("for Slurm on bigiron read bigiron/References/…"), a "Values at a glance" table and a list of the references with their paths (References/Access.md, bigiron/References/Slurm.md).
  • References/*.md hold the institution-wide facts (login and transfer hosts, off-campus access, accounts and two-factor sign-in, storage services, proxy quirks, documentation links), and <cluster>/References/*.md the facts of one cluster (partitions and GPU types, modules, driver/CUDA version, cluster paths). Keep the shell commands Claude Code users need. Links between reference files are relative (../bigiron/References/Slurm.md from References/Access.md); write the link text as the path from the skill folder ([bigiron/References/Slurm.md](../bigiron/References/Slurm.md)), which is also what Labmill's read_reference accepts.
  • Site.yaml and Cluster.yaml are described below. Claude Code ignores them.
  • Diagrams/ holds architecture drawings as SVG (plus a README.md describing them). They are neither embedded in Labmill nor served as skill references.

    • sites/generic/ is the profile for "My institution isn't listed". Its skill, site-generic, tells Claude how to find site facts without a profile (ask the user, read their documentation, query the cluster). It stays flat (no cluster folders); its _cluster-template/ folder is only a template to copy, and it gives sites/embed.go's cluster-folder patterns a file to match in a build with no other profiles.

items.title: Rules for facts
items.text:
• Every fact has a source: an official documentation URL, the upstream skill it came from, or a confirmed answer from the site. Put sources at the top of each reference file or next to the fact.
  • Anything not confirmed by an official page is marked (unverified).
  • Never guess a host name, project, partition or path. Leave it out (and the Site.yaml value empty) and add the question to the site's own sites/<domain>/QUESTIONS.md. Never log site questions or site facts in public files (docs/, commit messages).
  • No site term goes into public code or public files: not into skills/, sites/generic/, Go code or tests (tests use an example.edu fixture profile parsed with site.Parse/site.Load). internal/site's TestGenericSkillsHaveNoSiteFacts builds its forbidden terms from every embedded profile (domain, name, hostnames and their parent domains, aliases, cluster names and cluster folder names, URL hosts, plus the forbidden_terms of Site.yaml and of every Cluster.yaml) and scans skills/ and sites/generic/, so the test itself names no site. Add the terms it can't derive (project ids, bucket and asset names, short host names, version strings) to forbidden_terms: institution-wide terms in Site.yaml, a cluster's own terms in its Cluster.yaml.

items.title: Site.yaml
items.text:
domain: example.edu            # must equal the folder name ("generic" for the generic profile)
default: false                 # optional; true makes this the preselected choice in the first-run form (at most one profile; never generic)
name: Example University       # shown in the first-run choice
skill: site-example-edu        # must be "site-" + domain with dots as dashes
docs_url: https://hpc.example.edu/docs      # optional, https
broker_url: ""                 # optional Claude broker for this site; empty = call Anthropic directly with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
broker:
  issuers: []                  # optional: token issuers a broker maps to this profile; no issuer may be listed by two sites
two_factor:
  help: >-                     # shown when two-factor sign-in doesn't complete
    Example uses Duo. Enroll at https://it.example.edu/duo, then try again.
  url: https://it.example.edu/duo           # optional, https
  name: Duo                    # optional product name for prompts ("approve a Duo sign-in request"); omit for generic wording; plain text, <= 40 chars
s3_credentials_on_cluster: true  # optional; false turns off s3_credentials_to_cluster (copying one AWS profile to the login node); omitted = allowed
hosts:                         # SSH host templates for ~/.ssh/config.d/labmill
  - alias: ex-gw               # lowercase letters, digits, dashes
    hostname: gw.example.edu
    role: jump                 # login | transfer | jump
  - alias: ex-login
    hostname: login.example.edu
    role: login
    proxy_jump: ex-gw          # optional: another alias in this list
    port: 22                   # optional
    auth: password             # optional: password (default; keyboard-interactive + 2FA) | key (SSH keys only)
key_upload:                    # optional: where a new public key is registered, for hosts with auth: key
  url: https://reg.example.edu/keys          # https
  instruction: Open Profile, SSH keys, Add key, and paste the public key.   # one line, <= 300 chars
forbidden_terms:               # optional: extra terms that must never appear in the
  - "1234567"                  #   public skills (project ids, bucket names, short
  - ex-scratch                 #   host names, driver versions); at least 3 characters

Notes on some keys:

  • default: site.Default() returns the one profile with default: true, or generic when none sets it. A clusters.yaml without site: means that profile, and first-run setup preselects it. Two profiles marked default, or default on generic, is an error.
  • broker_url: when set (or when LABMILL_BROKER_URL is set), model calls go to that broker with the token from LABMILL_BROKER_TOKEN. When empty, the client calls the Anthropic Messages API with the user's own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
  • two_factor.name: the product name used in prompts ("approve a Duo sign-in request"). Omit it and the login dialog uses generic wording; Labmill's code names no product.
  • hosts[].auth and key_upload: a host with auth: key accepts SSH keys only. The first login there runs Labmill's key setup (see SSH): it looks for a usable key (a configured IdentityFile, the default ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, id_ecdsa, id_rsa, or an agent key) and otherwise creates an ed25519 key, shows the public key with key_upload.instruction and key_upload.url, waits for the user's confirmation and writes IdentityFile into ~/.ssh/config.d/labmill. key_upload is site-wide and optional; without it the dialog says to upload the key as the site's documentation describes. The values belong in the site skill's access reference too.
  • Reserved folder names: References, Evals, Diagrams and Tools are never cluster folders.

Unknown keys are an error, so typos surface. site.Parse checks the domain, the skill name, that URLs are https, that host aliases are unique and valid, that roles are known and that proxy_jump names a host in the file.

For older profiles Site.yaml still accepts clusters: (the same entries as Cluster.yaml, listed before the folder templates). New profiles put them in the cluster folders.

items.title: Cluster.yaml
items.text:
# sites/example.edu/bigiron/Cluster.yaml
name: bigiron
type: slurm
ssh_host: ex-login             # an alias from Site.yaml hosts
files_host: ex-files           # optional transfer-host alias
transfer: sftp
order: 0                       # optional: sort key among the site's clusters (below)
preemptible:                   # optional, Slurm only: the preemptible resource, if any
  partition: preempt           #   partition and/or qos (at least one); names [A-Za-z0-9._-]
  qos: ""                      #   e.g. lowprio
  requeue: true                #   jobs may be submitted with --requeue
  fallback_partition: ""       #   non-preemptible partition after the failed attempts; "" = the default
local_scratch:                 # optional, Slurm only: node-local disk on the compute nodes
  path: /tmp                   #   absolute folder or $VAR[/folder]; path or env_var is required
  env_var: TMPDIR              #   the variable the job finds its folder in; wins over path
  size_gb: 400                 #   0/omitted = unknown
global_scratch:                # optional, Slurm only: shared scratch on the compute nodes
  path: /scratch/<group>       #   absolute, clean; <placeholder> = the user's own part
  purge_days: 90               #   0/omitted = unknown
software_dir: /software/mygroup # optional, Slurm only: absolute clean folder for reusable environments (venv, conda, images); omitted = $HOME/.labmill/envs; not a purged scratch

site.ParseCluster rejects unknown keys and checks the template like a clusters.yaml entry; site.Load then checks that cluster names are unique across the site and that ssh_host and files_host name hosts in Site.yaml. preemptible, local_scratch, global_scratch and software_dir (rules.SlurmHints, checked by SlurmHints.Validate; software_dir is where draft_job's environment builds venvs, conda environments and SIF images) are only allowed on a Slurm cluster; unknown facts are left out, never guessed. Site.SlurmHintsFor(name) returns them; cluster_info states them in plain words and draft_job applies them (scratch, preemptible; see architecture.md). A Cluster.yaml with only comments (or none at all) declares no template: the folder then holds only references, for example while the login host is unconfirmed. Each file holds exactly one YAML document: a second one (after ---) is an error rather than silently ignored (the same for Site.yaml).

The cluster templates go to clusters.yaml in this order: Site.yaml's own clusters: (older profiles), then the cluster folders. Cluster.yaml's optional order: (an integer, default 0, negative allowed) sorts lower first, and equal values go by folder name. Use it to keep a site's main cluster first (the order of the prompt's configured clusters, list_clusters and the status line) when a smaller cluster's folder name sorts earlier.

Every value except domain, name and skill may be empty:

  • No login host: first-run setup asks the user for the login host and builds the hosts and clusters from it, as for the generic profile.
  • No broker: Labmill calls Anthropic directly with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; without that key each chat turn explains that the assistant isn't connected.
  • No two-factor help: the login dialog shows its generic text.

items.title: Naming
items.text:
• Names are lowercase: the institution folders (example.edu) and the cluster folders (bigcluster, and the placeholder _cluster-template).
  • Everything else starts with an uppercase letter and keeps the rest as written: folders (References, Evals, Diagrams) and files (Site.yaml, Cluster.yaml, Slurm.md, Hosts-and-access.md, Architecture.svg).
  • Exceptions: SKILL.md, README.md, QUESTIONS.md and SOURCE.md are already uppercase, and embed.go is Go source and stays lowercase.

TestSitesNaming in internal/site checks the profiles on disk, so a new profile follows the rule. Windows and macOS file systems ignore case, so never rely on two names that differ only in case.

items.title: How Labmill uses a site
items.text:
• sites/embed.go embeds every folder's Site.yaml, SKILL.md and References/*.md, and every cluster folder's Cluster.yaml and References/*.md (package sites). QUESTIONS.md, Evals/ and Diagrams/ stay out of the binary.
  • internal/site parses them: site.Get(domain), site.List() (the default first), site.Choices() (plus generic), site.Default() (the profile with default: true, or generic when none sets it), site.ForConfig(cfg) and site.Current(). LABMILL_BROKER_URL overrides the broker URL.
  • First-run setup (launch.Build with the front end's form) offers site.Choices(), then launch.WriteSetup writes the host templates to ~/.ssh/config.d/labmill (reusing the user's own aliases, rewriting ProxyJump to the final alias) and saves site: <domain> with the clusters to clusters.yaml. A config without site means the default site; an unknown site falls back to generic with a startup warning.
  • Other institutions. A session's home institution is the top-level site: of clusters.yaml. The other embedded profiles are known: site.Others(home) lists them, site.SkillsFSSession adds all their site skills to the home ones (a broken skill of another institution is a startup warning, only the home one is fatal), and the prompt names each with its clusters and skill. Work goes to the home institution unless the user explicitly names another; then add_cluster copies the cluster's Cluster.yaml template into clusters.yaml with a per-cluster site: <domain> (empty means the top-level site) and writes the SSH hosts it needs. A cluster with its own site: takes its hints, host_path, 2FA help and key-upload text from that institution's profile. Model calls stay the home institution's.
  • Site.SkillsFS(skills.FS) adds the site skill (SKILL.md, References/*.md, <cluster>/References/*.md) to the generic skills under its own name, so load_skill can load it. The skill runtime lists a cluster folder's references as <cluster>/<file>.md (e.g. bigiron/Slurm.md), and read_reference also accepts the path inside the skill (bigiron/References/Slurm.md, or ../bigiron/References/Slurm.md as written in a link from another reference). The system prompt names the site and tells Claude to load the site skill for site facts and never guess.

items.title: Adding a site, step by step
items.text:
1. Create sites/<domain>/ with Site.yaml, SKILL.md, at least one References/*.md and a QUESTIONS.md for what you couldn't confirm, following the rules above. Add one folder per cluster (copy sites/generic/_cluster-template/) with its Cluster.yaml and references, and index the folders in SKILL.md.
  2. Run go test ./internal/site/ ./internal/skill/: TestEmbeddedSites loads every profile and its skill next to the generic skills, and TestGenericSkillsHaveNoSiteFacts checks that none of the new site's terms are in the public skills.
  3. Try it in Claude Code: copy the generic skills and the whole site folder, cluster folders included (as site-<domain-with-dashes>), into ~/.claude/skills/ (see sites/README.md) and ask a site question.
  4. Keep the new profile out of this repository: .gitignore ignores every sites/<domain>/ folder except sites/generic/.

items.title: SSH login and OpenSSH config (design decisions)
items.text:
The full design of the one-time SSH login, Labmill's own connection sharing and the OpenSSH config file. CLAUDE.md keeps a short summary. The implementation is in Architecture ("SSH helper and ssh-exec", "SSH config files").

Audience: researchers who already run code successfully on their own Mac or Windows computer, often on a single local GPU, and now need to scale out. They don't know the cluster environment, often don't know containers well, and want a chat interface to run their jobs. Nothing may assume they know the terminal, SSH or ~/.ssh/config.

Go-native SSH (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh) on every platform. Don't shell out to ssh. Labmill doesn't reuse the user's terminal SSH sessions. It runs its own login and its own multiplexing.

  • First login is a GUI/TUI dialog that looks like a normal SSH login.
  • Labmill asks for the username, then the password (keyboard-interactive auth).
  • When the server shows the 2FA menu (Duo-style, e.g. Passcode or option (1-3):), Labmill picks the "Duo Push" option itself (usually 1; the number is read from the menu, since phone-only users may have a call or SMS there) and tells the user to approve it on their phone. Some servers push without any menu, so after the password any wait is treated as a 2FA wait, with the push timeout armed. 2b. The push notice always clears. Prompter.Notify("") means "clear the status line". sshx.login sends it on every way out once it showed a push notice (success, failure, timeout, cancel), and sshx.Connect does the same for notices relayed from the helper, so a front end never keeps "Approve the sign-in request ..." after the wait ended. A helper that already holds the login relays no notice at all. The GUI's labmill:notify event with empty text and the TUI's NotifyMsg clear the line.
  • If no push arrives (timeout, or the server says the user isn't enrolled), show instructions for setting up 2FA. Make the enrollment link and text configurable per site rather than hardcoded. 3b. Lockout safety. Some institutions lock an account (e-mail too) after a few failed password logins. Labmill never resubmits a password by itself, and a password that was sent and rejected without any 2FA step (ErrPasswordRejected, which wraps ErrAuthDenied and has its own helper relay code password) now ends with the site's two_factor.help (when there is one) and sshx.PasswordCareNote: "Check your password before trying again: many institutions lock the account after repeated failed sign-ins." When no password was ever sent (for example a key-only host not flagged as such), the failure stays a plain ErrAuthDenied with neutral text ("the server accepted none of the offered sign-in methods") and no advice about the password. 2FA failures (ErrTwoFactor) keep their own message. The system prompt tells Claude to stop after such a result, explain it and wait for the user. In code, connCache.client records a host whose login ended in ErrPasswordRejected, together with the other hosts of the same institution (the cluster's ssh_host and files_host, siblingHosts, computed from the live config so a cluster added later counts; they share the account; a sibling is refused with "a sign-in at this institution failed a moment ago; check your password, then ask me to try again"), and, until the next turn (Session.Send runs connCache.newTurn), refuses a new login to it with "sign-in to failed a moment ago; check your password, then ask me to try again" without dialing. 2FA and network failures do not arm the guard.
  • Let the user type a passcode instead if they prefer.
  • Key-only sites (no password login) get a guided key setup instead of the password dialog. The guide first reuses a key the host already accepts: QueryKeys asks the host about public keys only (the RFC 4252 public-key query, which stops before any signature), for local key files not offered at sign-in (the agent's keys were already offered by Dial) and, over a connection that is already open, the home cluster's keys (ListRemoteKeys). An accepted key that exists only on the home node is copied to a new 0600 file after an approval dialog that defaults to No and is never auto-approved. If nothing is accepted, it creates a new key and uploads it per the site's instructions. See Architecture ("Guided setup"). 5b. Key query batching and host limiting (keyquery.go, keyreuse.go). Every rejected key in a query counts toward the server's MaxAuthTries, and OpenSSH 9.8+ penalizes a source after failed logins by closing new connections before the handshake. So QueryKeys offers several keys on one connection (ssh.PublicKeys with the query signers), at most maxKeysPerConn (5) per connection, and fewer after a "too many authentication failures" disconnect. It pauses queryPause (7 s, longer than the 5 s penalty; tests shorten it) between connections and returns the results gathered so far instead of nothing when a later connection fails. A host that closes before the handshake gives ErrHostLimiting (wrapped with the host name). When no key has been accepted yet, KeyGuide.useExistingKey then notifies, waits limitWait (a minute), and asks once more only the keys not yet asked. If the host still limits, it returns an error ending "is still refusing connections; wait a few minutes and try again" and does not go on to create a new key (the user would register one they may not need). A key accepted before the failure still counts.
  • Several institutions in one session. LoginOptions.Hosts maps a lowercase host name to its own HostLogin (2FA help and name), so each host shows its institution's 2FA text; the plain fields apply to every other host. The jump chain (dialChain) and the host key question (hostKeyCheck) are shared by Dial and QueryKeys, so a key query never accepts an unknown host silently either.
  • Labmill's own ControlMaster. One authenticated connection carries everything: commands run as separate sessions on it, and SFTP runs on it. Each process gets that from x/crypto/ssh for free. To share the connection across processes (TUI, GUI and Agent) and keep it alive briefly after Labmill exits, the first Labmill process starts a small helper that holds the connection. The helper listens on a per-user local socket (a Unix socket, or AF_UNIX on Windows 10+), and exits after about 10 minutes idle, like OpenSSH ControlPersist. Later Labmill processes connect to the socket instead of logging in again. Before the helper hands a held login to a new client (also to ConnectCached), it checks that the login still answers a keepalive request within the keepalive timeout (15 s), unless a keepalive answered within the last keepalive interval (30 s; measured on the wall clock, so time spent suspended counts). A login that doesn't answer (the laptop slept, the network changed) is dropped and its local clients closed, and the client gets a fresh login with its prompts (ConnectCached gets ErrNotConnected). A busy but working link is never dropped this way while its keepalives answer. A local client's own keepalive request is answered only once the cluster login answered one, so a caller can tell a stale login (drop the cached connection, connect again) from a merely slow command (keep it). Commands on a held connection honor their context also while the session opens (backend.SSHRunner), so a stale link times out instead of hanging.
  • SSH settings are kept in OpenSSH format, so the user can switch to a plain terminal later. Users may later want direct terminal access, so every SSH setting Labmill creates goes in an OpenSSH-compatible config file, and ssh <alias> / sftp <alias> simply works afterwards. This file is the single source of truth: Labmill reads its own connections from it, and clusters.yaml only refers to the alias.
  • Labmill owns ~/.ssh/config.d/labmill (on Windows, %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config.d\labmill). It adds one Include config.d/labmill line at the top of ~/.ssh/config. The top matters because an Include placed after a Host/Match block only applies inside that block. If ~/.ssh/config is missing, create it, with ~/.ssh at 0700 and the files at 0600. Back up the existing file before the one-line edit, and never rewrite the user's own entries.
  • Directives written per host: Host <alias>, HostName, User, Port if it isn't 22, ProxyJump when there's a jump host, and ServerAliveInterval. On macOS/Linux also write ControlMaster auto, ControlPath ~/.ssh/controlmasters/%r@%h:%p (create that directory) and ControlPersist 10m, so later terminal use gets the same one-login behavior. Leave those three out on Windows, where Win32-OpenSSH errors on them.
  • Aliases: OpenSSH uses the first value it finds for each setting, and the Include sits at the top. If the user already has a Host entry for that hostname, reuse their alias instead of adding one. Otherwise pick an alias that doesn't clash with any of their entries.
  • The Go side parses this file plus the user's ~/.ssh/config with a Go ssh_config parser (check that it follows Include). It honors HostName, User, Port, ProxyJump and IdentityFile, and ignores directives it can't act on (Match … Exec, ControlMaster; Labmill's helper does that job).
  • Bastion vs. login host. At many sites the bastion is the Slurm login host, so it's a single hop. Where the login/submit host sits behind a separate bastion, Labmill does a ProxyJump.
  • x/crypto/ssh has no ProxyJump setting, but it supports the mechanism directly: dial the next hop over the existing connection (client.Dial("tcp", "login:22")), then run ssh.NewClientConn on that net.Conn. Chain this for several hops.
  • Each hop can need its own login, so the dialog may run once per hop.
  • The jump host is recorded as ProxyJump in the cluster's OpenSSH entry (see above), so terminal ssh takes the same route.

items.title: Interactive shell
items.text:
labmill shell <cluster> [--dir <folder>] and the TUI's /shell <cluster> [--dir <folder>] open a shell on the login node over a new session of the helper's existing connection (sshx.RunShell: RequestPty with the local TERM (default xterm-256color) and size, then Shell, or with --dir the command cd -- <quoted dir> && exec $SHELL -l; window-change on resize: SIGWINCH on Unix, polling every 300 ms on Windows). sshx.ShellExec puts the local terminal in raw mode (golang.org/x/term; on Windows it also turns on VT input and output processing), restores it on every exit path including SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and reads stdin through a poll reader so no key typed after the shell ends is swallowed. It implements Bubble Tea's ExecCommand, so the TUI suspends with tea.Exec and resumes when the shell exits. The open session is a local connection to the helper, so its idle timer does not fire while a shell is open. Login prompts for a missing sign-in use the usual path (TUI: the login modal through the Bridge and the key setup; CLI: a terminal prompter that asks once and never retries a password). Privacy: the shell's bytes are never logged, shown in the chat or sent to Claude; labmill.log gets "shell opened/closed on " only.

Desktop terminal. The Wails app shows the same session in xterm.js tabs (internal/gui/terminal.go, frontend/terminal.js). PageAPI.OpenTerminal(cluster, dir, cols, rows) and OpenJobTerminal(jobID, cols, rows) (the folder comes from the job store, never from the page; the cluster and folder may not contain \n, \r or NUL) return an ID at once; launch.Runtime.RunTerminal then connects through the helper (the same forgetDenied/markDenied handling as OpenShell, so a missing sign-in shows the normal login dialog once), runs sshx.RunShell with the xterm.js size and closes its connection when the shell ends. Events to the page: labmill:term-out {id, data} (base64 of raw bytes, chunks of at most 16 KB, in order), labmill:term-state {id, state:"open"}, labmill:term-exit {id, code, message}. From the page: TerminalInput(id, seq, base64) (never blocks: typing before the connection is up is queued, 1 MB at most; bigger input fails with "paste too large"), TerminalResize(id, seq, cols, rows), TerminalAck(id, n), CloseTerminal(id) (no exit event). Ordering: Wails runs every bound call in its own goroutine, so the page sends one input call at a time (what is typed meanwhile is joined into the next call) and one resize at a time (newest size wins), and Go delivers input by sequence number (a reorder buffer of up to 64 calls; a rejected call still uses its number) and ignores a resize older than one already seen. Flow control: output stalls once 256 KB are unacknowledged; the page acknowledges what term.write has finished (batched every 10 ms), so a slow page pauses the stdout copy, the SSH window fills and the remote program waits; closing a terminal wakes a stalled writer. Sign-in: while a chat turn runs (gui.App.Busy) a terminal opens no dialog and clears no refusal; it uses a login the helper already holds (sshx.ConnectCached) or shows "Sign-in is possible once the assistant has finished; try again then" in its tab. Otherwise terminal connects to one host are serialized (terminalClient): the first clears an old refusal like /shell, a request that waited behind it does not and, if the password was rejected meanwhile, fails with the refusal instead of prompting; the page disables New terminal while a tab is connecting. At most 8 terminals; Terminals.CloseAll runs at shutdown. The connection to the helper stays open while a terminal exists, so the helper's idle timer does not fire. "Open in system terminal" (internal/gui/systerm.go) starts x-terminal-emulator/gnome-terminal/konsole/xfce4-terminal/xterm (Linux, the command wrapped in sh -c with the program and cluster as positional parameters), wt.exe or, without it, the CLI itself with CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE (Windows, systerm_windows.go; no cmd) or Terminal.app through osascript running exec /bin/sh -c '<script>' sh <cli> <cluster> (macOS; also for fish users) with labmill shell <cluster>; the cluster name must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@-]*. The labmill binary is looked for next to the GUI binary (labmill or labmill-<GOOS>-<GOARCH>, .exe required on Windows; also beside a macOS .app), then on the PATH; the option is hidden when it isn't found. Privacy: the terminal's bytes only travel between Go and the page (no logging, no chat, no Claude); labmill.log gets "terminal opened/closed on " only. Vendored (MIT, license files beside them in frontend/vendor/xterm/): @xterm/xterm 6.0.0 (xterm.js, xterm.css) and @xterm/addon-fit 0.11.0 (addon-fit.js), copied unmodified from the npm packages; to upgrade, fetch the new lib/*.js, css/xterm.css and LICENSE files the same way and update these versions. xterm.js writes <style> elements for its layout and colors, so the page's Content-Security-Policy has style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (style attributes and scripts stay locked to 'self'; nothing in the page builds markup from untrusted text).

Details of the terminal handling. On Windows the console input is read as console input records (ReadConsoleInputW, key-down records with a character only, so a key-up or mouse record can never block a read and swallow the first key typed after the shell ends; Ctrl+Z is data). ShellExec.Run closes the input, waits for the read in flight (guardedReader) and only then restores the terminal. SIGTERM or SIGHUP while a shell is open ends it, restores the terminal and returns *sshx.ErrShellSignaled: the TUI quits, and labmill shell exits with 128 plus the signal number. A channel that closes without an exit status (dropped connection) is sshx.ErrShellClosed: labmill shell prints "the connection to closed" and exits 255. An explicit /shell clears only the "password rejected" refusal of its own host and the institution's other hosts (connCache.forgetDenied), never other institutions' refusals or the canceled-sign-in flag, and is still one login attempt.
